name: Chemal Hydropower Plant and Patmos Island
full: Two neighbouring sights in the village of Chemal at the confluence of the Chemal and Katun: the historic Chemal hydropower plant (1935, 16A Kedrovaya St.) and the rocky island of Patmos on the Katun with the Church of St. John the Theologian, linked to the shore by a suspension bridge; between them runs the pedestrian “Goat Trail” (~1 km).
near: The village of Chemal (the sights are within the village); Gorno-Altaysk ~95–98 km (bolshayastrana).
short: Chemal's most popular pair of sights: the first hydropower plant in the Altai Mountains (1935), now a museum with a dam, viewpoints and attractions, and Patmos Island with its wooden Church of St. John the Theologian, reached by a swaying suspension bridge over the turquoise Katun.
desc: The Chemal hydropower plant was built in 1935 by prisoners (~700 people, trekkingmania) — the first hydropower plant in the Altai Republic; construction ran 1931–1935 (privet-altai), with a capacity of ~400 kW (privet-altai), <460 kW (220+240 kW, trekkingmania) or 500 kW (welcometoaltai), depending on the source; it survived the floods of 1959 and 1969 and supplied nearby villages and sanatoriums. In 2011, after an accident/flooding of the machine hall, the plant was shut down, in 2013 the reservoir was drained, and the 2014 flood damaged the earthen part of the dam and the bridge (sibalt). Now it is a monument of local significance and a museum: in summer — tours of the plant building, a paid walk onto the dam, and all around a souvenir market, an extreme-entertainment park (a bungee swing, the “Krutoe Pike” (Steep Dive), a zip line, a Ferris wheel), and ATV and catamaran rentals. About 300 m away is the confluence of the Chemal and Katun. Patmos Island is a rock in the Katun in the centre of Chemal, consecrated in 1855 in honour of the Apostle John the Theologian (by analogy with the Greek Patmos). The church built on the island in 1915 burned down in the 1920s–30s; in the 1990s the Muscovite Viktor Pavlov restored the shrine, in 1998 a suspension bridge was built (about 15 m above the water), and in 2000 a new cedar church of about 20 m², consecrated on 10.01.2001 (kp.ru, bolshayastrana). Today the island holds the women's skete of the Apostle John the Theologian of the Barnaul Znamensky Monastery (altaitur.com); on the rock is a carved image of the Mother of God. Entry to the island is free, donations are welcome; since 2020 vehicle access to the island has been closed by a barrier. Between the hydropower plant and the island, the “Goat Trail” runs along the Katun (~1 km, partly with wooden stairs).
guide: Come before 9 a.m. — after that there is a queue on the suspension bridge to Patmos, and the bridge sways noticeably (you may feel dizzy if you're not used to it). Speak quietly on the island: it is a working women's skete, and women are better off bringing a scarf and a skirt. Find the image of the Mother of God carved into the rock by the nuns, and watch from the island as the Katun changes colour from turquoise to milky. Then walk the “Goat Trail” over the rocks along the Katun to the old hydropower plant — the 1935 dam, built by prisoners, is now overgrown with attractions, but the plant itself is a piece of history. If you want quiet — come in September.
see: The suspension bridge and Patmos Island; the Church of St. John the Theologian (cedar, a myrrh-streaming icon — kp.ru); the image of the Mother of God on the rock; viewpoints over the Katun; the “Goat Trail” Patmos — hydropower plant (~1 km); the dam and machine hall of the hydropower plant (a museum, tours in summer); the confluence of the Chemal and Katun (~300 m from the hydropower plant, free; ~200 m for the entrance — gorniy-altai 2020); nearby — the trail to the Tekelyu waterfall, the Chemal highway along the Katun.
skip: You don't like crowds and souvenir stalls — in summer by day this is one of the most crowded corners of the Altai; or you're afraid of heights and wobbly bridges.
diff: Easy: the bridge and island — 30–40 min (vsesvoitravel); the “Goat Trail” — moderate, with narrow spots above a drop, but passable with children (sibalt).
when: May — September; September — fewer people and soft light (sredi-gor). In winter the bridge is slippery/dangerous (bolshayastrana).
hours: The island — round the clock (kp.ru); the Church of St. John the Theologian — 2GIS (address 74 Sovetskaya St.): in winter Mon–Sun 9:00–17:00, summer hours not given; the hydropower plant — tours inside the building only in the tourist season (2GIS, altai.travel); hours not found.
daytime: Early morning (before 9:00) — no queue for the bridge (sredi-gor); evening — soft light on the Katun.
how: From Gorno-Altaysk along the Chuysky Trakt (R256 highway) to Ust-Sema and then along the Chemal highway to the village of Chemal (~95–98 km, ~2 h). Buses Gorno-Altaysk — Chemal: 06:25, 13:35, 14:05, 16:25, 18:30, 1 h 55 min – 2 h, from 720–750 ₽ (e-traffic 2026). Novosibirsk — Chemal: 8 trips 07:40–22:20, 9 h 40 min – 11 h 12 min, from 4132 ₽ (Avtotranssib, sole proprietor Shpilekov; avtovokzaly 2026). Barnaul — Chemal (return 07:20 and 14:45, from 2400 ₽, e-traffic). The Chemal bus station — 1a Sovetskaya St.; from the centre to the bridge ~15 min on foot (kp.ru).
needcar: To Chemal — yes (bus/car); around Chemal — on foot.
roadtype: Paved up to Chemal (the Chemal highway); to the bridge — pedestrian streets and trails; the “Goat Trail” — dirt, rocks, wooden stairs.
traveltime: Gorno-Altaysk — Chemal ~2 h by bus; Novosibirsk — Chemal ~10–11 h; on site — 4–5 h for everything (sredi-gor).
stay: Chemal (101hotels 2026): the “Altai Voyage” guesthouse from 2500 ₽ (9.3, 100 m from the centre), the “Faraonova Dacha” (Pharaoh's Dacha) mini-hotel from 3500 ₽ (9.1), “CheKaGo” from 5850 ₽ (10.0), the “Solntse Altaya” (Altai Sun) holiday base from 6000 ₽ (9.6); guesthouses by the hydropower plant from 1700 ₽ (welcometoaltai, year not specified).
net: Chemal has mobile signal and internet (a large village) — specific operators not checked.
entry: Patmos — free, donations (kp.ru, bolshayastrana). The hydropower plant (okolo.city, a 2026 page): the dam 100 ₽, the machine-hall museum 200 ₽ (a guided tour only, included in the ticket — privet-altai: 150–200 ₽), parking 100 ₽; the bungee swing 800 ₽ (2023, privet-altai). Earlier: a walk onto the dam ~100 ₽, the museum 150–200 ₽, parking ~100 ₽ (sredi-gor, year not specified; gorniy-altai 15.07.2020 — the dam 100 ₽, parking 100 ₽ cash only). Attractions 300–500 ₽, the Ferris wheel 200 ₽.
transfer: A bus Gorno-Altaysk — Chemal from 720 ₽ (2026); a tour from 2500 ₽/person; a private tour from 21,500 ₽/group (2026).
bring: Comfortable shoes with non-slip soles (the Goat Trail), a scarf/covered clothing for the church, cash (hydropower plant parking is cash only, 2020), water, tick repellent.
warn: The suspension bridge sways — hold on to children, don't take photos while walking, queues in summer. The Goat Trail has narrow spots above a drop. Swimming in the Katun is dangerous — a strong, cold current. Ticks in May–July (in the Altai Republic by 25.08.2026 — 3600 bite reports). Vehicles are not allowed to the island (a barrier since 2020). A working skete — keep quiet and follow the dress code.
food: Chemal (2GIS 2026): “Chemalskoe Podvorye” (4.9/682, maral (Altai deer) dishes, a bill of ~850 ₽), “Lesnoy” (4.9/804, Altai cuisine, ~1600 ₽), “Ku-Kukhnya” (4.9/383, a view of the Katun, ~1500 ₽), “Skazka” (5.0/230, home cooking, ~800 ₽).
reviews: 2GIS: Patmos Island 4.7/5 (1082 ratings, 374 reviews); the Church of St. John the Theologian 4.9/5 (253 ratings); the Chemal hydropower plant 3.9/5 (220 ratings, 179 reviews) — 2026. Patmos pros: atmosphere, views, the bridge; cons: crowds, dizziness on the bridge. Hydropower plant: history, the confluence of the rivers; cons — commercialization, attractions, fees.

p.sum: Patmos and the Chemal hydropower plant are in the centre of Chemal, ~2 h by bus from Gorno-Altaysk (from 720 ₽). The island is free; at the hydropower plant the dam is ~100 ₽, the museum 150–200 ₽, parking ~100 ₽. Between them is the Goat Trail, ~1 km. Come before 9:00.
